title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency and throughput benchmarks vs the baseline provider. Redwood team walked through tuned configs (batching, kv-cache, quantization), showed 20-35% token-cost improvement on tail latency under representative load, and identified next steps: run end-to-end test with NovaHealth dataset, share benchmark spreadsheet, and schedule a canary run on dedicated pool. Customer flagged logging/audit and SSO questions; Redwood to share security docs and rollback playbook.
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs link by 2026-04-09
NovaHealth: provide representative dataset subset for e2e by 2026-04-10
Schedule canary run on dedicated pool w/c 2026-04-13 - Sam to propose times
Redwood to send security docs (SOC2, infra diagram, audit log sample)
action_items: Sam Lee: email benchmark spreadsheet + raw logs link - due 2026-04-09
Priya Nair: prepare recommended config (batch size, kv cache TTL, quantization profile) - due 2026-04-10
Mike Chen: share 5k-row representative input set for e2e - due 2026-04-10
Rohit Kumar: confirm network egress/peering constraints for dedicated - due 2026-04-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sam Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood Solutions), Aisha Patel (CTO, NovaHealth), Mike Chen (Eng Lead), Rohit Kumar (Infra), Leah Gomez (PM)

Auto-generated summary: weekly benchmark review, compare to baseline provider, next steps for pilot canary.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sam Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, i see folks on the call, quick roll call?
[00:07] Aisha Patel: hi Aisha here, CTO, thanks Sam
[00:10] Mike Chen: mike here, eng lead
[00:12] Rohit Kumar: rohit infra
[00:14] Leah Gomez: leah product
[00:18] Sam Lee: perfect, ok so agenda - quick recap of last week's runs, latency/throughput numbers vs baseline, tuning changes we applied, and then agree next steps, any additions?
[00:27] Priya Nair: i want to call out the tail latency graphs, we dug into 95th and 99th, and there's some interesting behavior when bursty requests hit the kv cache miss path
[00:35] Aisha Patel: yes please emphasise tail, for us user-facing latency matters more than median
[00:39] Sam Lee: totally, cool. i'll share screen now with the benchmark deck - can everyone see?
[00:46] Mike Chen: yep looking
[00:48] Sam Lee: ok slide 3 is baseline summary - baseline provider measured on their managed endpoint, 8 v100 equiv, default batching, no prefix cache. average p50 token latency about 11ms, p95 78ms, p99 210ms under our synthetic load.
[01:10] Priya Nair: and our first pass (untuned) on the same HW profile showed similar median but worse tail because of cold kv cache behavior, so we applied continuous batching and prefix kv cache to reduce the p95/p99
[01:24] Sam Lee: slide 6 shows tuned run - we enabled adaptive batching with max batch 32, kv cache TTL 300s for repeated sessions, and int8 quantization on the weights for this model variant. Results: p50 9ms, p95 58ms, p99 145ms, throughput ~380 reqs/s.
[01:42] Mike Chen: wait quantization improved tail? surprised, we expected perf hit for int8 on a few ops
[01:47] Priya Nair: yeah good question, so int8 reduced memory bandwidth and improved kernel cache usage, but we did tune kernel selection and added a fallback for problematic ops - so on aggregate it reduced end-to-end token time. we also saw lower GPU memory pressure which helps throughput.
[02:05] Rohit Kumar: were these runs on hosted or dedicated infra?
[02:09] Sam Lee: these were in our dedicated bench pool configured to mirror your proposed dedicated setup - single-tenant-ish, same networking. we can run hosted vs dedicated comparison if you want.
[02:18] Aisha Patel: can we see the raw logs for p99 spikes? need to understand if it's network or model compute
[02:23] Sam Lee: yes we'll share the raw run logs and the per-token breakdown - you'll see network vs gpu decode vs kv lookup columns.
[02:31] Priya Nair: quick note - most p99 now is kv cache misses + small serialization overhead when we do a cold session; when we prepopulate cache for common prefixes it drops significantly.
[02:43] Leah Gomez: how much engineering lift to prepopulate cache from our side?
[02:47] Priya Nair: minimal - you can seed the cache via a warmup API call or we can replay the first N requests in a warmup job, we can provide a script.
[02:56] Sam Lee: slide 9 compares cost per 1M tokens - baseline provider estimated $X (anonymized), Redwood tuned path shows ~20-35% lower token cost when batching and cache active.
[03:10] Mike Chen: the cost calc assumes your quantization profile - what's the quality delta? our product is sensitive to hallucinations
[03:17] Priya Nair: we ran a small eval set (2k prompts) comparing top-k truncation and int8 quant; quality delta was within 0.5-1% on our rubric, we can run your exact eval suite.
[03:28] Aisha Patel: please do - we need to ensure the regression is negligible on our prompts
[03:31] Sam Lee: agreed.
[03:33] Carlos Rivera: jumping in, we also instrumented token-level tracing so you can see which tokens triggered kv misses or fallback kernels; that will be in the spreadsheet.
[04:10] Mike Chen: good. can you remind me of the security/audit capabilities? we have strict log retention and SSO requirements
[04:16] Sam Lee: yes - SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integrations. we'll send our security pack (diagram, SOC2 report redacted, example audit logs), and we'll call out where logs live in dedicated vs hosted.
[04:29] Rohit Kumar: for dedicated, we need private peering and customer-managed KMS. is that supported?
[04:34] Priya Nair: yes both supported. dedicated deployment supports VPC peering and bring-your-own-kms/HSM, with audit trails forwarded to your logging account.
[04:42] Leah Gomez: back to perf, did you try workload with longer context lengths? our product sometimes pushes 4k tokens
[04:48] Priya Nair: we ran 1k and 4k samples; at 4k the throughput drops as expected but batching and kv cache still helped reduce per-token cost; tail latency worsens with naive batching so we used smaller max batch for long-context runs.
[05:05] Mike Chen: any examples of tradeoff configs you recommend for 4k?
[05:09] Priya Nair: yes - for 4k we suggested max batch 12, increase kv cache TTL, and selective quantization (leave attention weights fp16). we'll document exact profiles.
[05:20] Sam Lee: ok moving to canary/run strategy - propose a canary on your dedicated pool with 5% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor p95/p99, errors, and quality. automatic fallback to baseline provider if regressions exceed thresholds.
[05:36] Aisha Patel: fallback policy is key - what's the mechanism and RTO?
[05:39] Sam Lee: automated routing policy - if error rate > 1% or p99 increase > 2x baseline for 10 minutes, traffic auto-fails over. typical recovery <5 minutes if it's routing. we'll share the playbook.
[05:55] Rohit Kumar: how are secrets managed for dedicated?
[05:57] Carlos Rivera: secrets are stored in customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed with strict access controls, RBAC, and audit logs. we'll include a diagram of key flow.
[06:10] Mike Chen: curious about comparison to BaselineAI - they do a lot of caching at the application layer; are we seeing different behavior?
[06:17] Priya Nair: BaselineAI's caching is more request level; our kv-style prefix cache is token-level which yields better reuse for multi-turn chat. in some patterns BaselineAI might look better for simple single-shot calls but falters on multi-turn.
[06:36] Sam Lee: we ran a side-by-side for the NovaHealth prompt set - median similar, but on multi-turn throughput we saw 15-25% better throughput and 20-40% better p99 vs BaselineAI when cache used. details in sheet.
[07:20] Mike Chen: about the benchmark rig - what's the synthetic load profile? is it realistic to our traffic?
[07:25] Priya Nair: we used a mixed poisson arrival with bursts to emulate your diurnal spikes, with 60% single-shot and 40% multi-turn conversations; we can re-run with your production trace if you share it.
[07:40] Aisha Patel: we'll share a 24h sample trace, obfuscated.
[07:45] Priya Nair: tuning note - network serialization overhead was a bigger fraction on smaller payloads; using a binary protocol reduced overhead by ~12% in microbenchmarks.
[08:12] Mike Chen: do you support gRPC? we prefer gRPC for lower overhead
[08:15] Sam Lee: yes gRPC supported, and websockets for streaming. we'll provide examples.
[08:23] Leah Gomez: regarding costs, is the 20-35% improvement on the full stack including infra and data transfer?
[08:28] Carlos Rivera: yes that calc includes token compute, model infra, and an estimated egress; exact numbers will vary by region and your network egress pricing.
[08:40] Mike Chen: for SLA - what uptime guarantee do you offer for dedicated?
[08:44] Sam Lee: dedicated has SLA options in the enterprise contract - we'll surface the SLA table in the proposal doc.
[09:05] Aisha Patel: any GDPR or data residency concerns? we have EU users and need logs in-region
[09:09] Sam Lee: we have region controls and can ensure logs and backups stay in-region for Private deployments; we'll include data residency notes in the security pack.
[09:20] Mike Chen: ok good. next - debug artifacts, about the raw logs link - will that contain PII?
[09:25] Carlos Rivera: we'll sanitize and provide redacted logs; for e2e you'll provide obfuscated sample inputs.
[09:32] Sam Lee: quick pause - any blockers for running the canary next week?
[09:36] Rohit Kumar: network peering still pending sign-off from our cloud team, and we need to confirm KMS approach
[09:41] Aisha Patel: security review needs to happen but not blocker for canary if logs are redacted and we use a test dataset
[09:47] Sam Lee: ok we'll treat network peering as an action item for Rohit, and Sam will provide runbook for canary and rollback.
[09:55] Priya Nair: also will prepare the specific config profiles: short-context (<=1k) and long-context (4k) and the recommended batch sizes and quantization toggles.
[10:22] Mike Chen: can you also include a perf run that matches our peak concurrency (we see 800 concurrent users during peak)?
[10:27] Priya Nair: yes we'll run a peak-concurrency profile.
[10:30] Sam Lee: ok going to the Q&A, any other concerns?
[10:33] Leah Gomez: curious about cost predictability if usage grows 5x - can Redwood offer committed capacity?
[10:38] Sam Lee: yes Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity is available; we can draft a sizing and pricing model if you expect sustained growth.
[10:47] Aisha Patel: timeline - we want to decide on pilot expansion by end of month.
[10:51] Sam Lee: noted.
[10:53] Carlos Rivera: final note - we'll include the token-level traces, benchmark spreadsheet, and the canary runbook in the follow-up email.
[11:10] Sam Lee: recap of action items and next steps. thanks everyone.
[11:18] Aisha Patel: thanks all
[11:20] Mike Chen: thanks
[11:22] Meeting end.
